notes: Overall a solid implementation with clear separation of concerns. Issues found: (1) ARCHITECTURAL - UserService and ProjectService receive no EventBus instance and never publish events, which means no events fire for user/project mutations; this is acceptable per spec but ProjectService has no event integration at all. More critically, the NotificationService for comment.added relies on assigneeId being passed through the HTTP request body rather than the TaskService owning that data — this is a subtle but real architectural violation: the router/client is bridging data between services instead of the event bus carrying complete context derived from service-owned data. The TaskService should publish assigneeId from its own store; instead the comment creation endpoint requires the caller to pass assigneeId, meaning the client is acting as a service-to-service mediator. (2) CONSTRAINT VIOLATION - Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is technically honored, but the workaround of passing task context (assigneeId, taskTitle) through the HTTP body is a design smell that circumvents the spirit of the rule. The CommentService should only know about the comment; enrichment for notifications should come from the TaskService reacting to comment.added or the EventBus carrying that context from TaskService. (3) The EventBus uses setImmediate for async delivery, which means notifications are not guaranteed to be present when the demo immediately queries them after posting a comment — the demo adds a workaround via sequential awaits but there is a real race condition. (4) GET /tasks without projectId returns empty array rather than all tasks, which is an incomplete implementation. (5) No input validation (missing required fields like name/email on user creation, title on task creation) — services will create malformed entities silently. (6) Error responses from services (e.g., null returns, error objects from changeStatus) are returned with HTTP 200 instead of 404/400, conflating success and failure at the HTTP layer. (7) node-shims.d.ts is unnecessary overhead and somewhat fragile. (8) The custom type declaration for 'http' module shadows the real @types/node declarations in a potentially confusing way. (9) UUID uses Math.random which is noted but acceptable per the demo disclaimer. (10) No unsubscribe mechanism on EventBus could cause memory leaks in longer-lived instances. Code is generally clean and readable with good TypeScript typing.
